pathogen.value: Duck Atadenovirus A (also called duck adenovirus 1)

value: passed from hen to chick before hatching
spread through eggs and droppings once mature birds start shedding virus

mortality.value: Increased mortality is not typically seen with this disease

diagnosis.value: Clinical signs plus lab tests such as antibody blood tests or PCR, since it can look similar to other poultry diseases

value: cleaning and disinfecting breeding and laying areas and egg trays
keeping healthy flocks separate from infected birds or wild waterfowl
vaccinating pullets before they start laying

treatment_overview.value: There is no treatment once a flock is infected; management relies on prevention and vaccination

summary.value: Egg drop syndrome is a viral infection of chickens and waterfowl that causes a sudden decline in egg output and poor shell quality without normally raising deaths. It spreads through infected eggs, droppings, and shared equipment, and is managed mainly through hygiene and vaccination since there is no cure.
